children: Zellmer will take over from Håkan Samuelsson no later than 1 October 2027, with the company planning a transition period

Volvo Cars has appointed Klaus Zellmer as its new President and Chief Executive Officer. He will assume the role no later than 1 October 2027, with current CEO Håkan Samuelsson and the Board of Directors overseeing the transition.

Zellmer has more than 30 years of experience in the automotive industry and currently serves as Chairman of the Board of Management and CEO of Škoda Auto. Before joining Škoda, he was a member of the Board of Management of Volkswagen Passenger Cars, responsible for marketing, sales and after-sales operations.
Zellmer spent more than two decades at Porsche, where he held several senior positions, including CEO of Porsche Deutschland and CEO of Porsche North America.

He began his professional career in the automotive sector in 1994 at the Institute for Automotive Economics at Nürtingen-Geislingen University of Applied Sciences, after completing a degree in business administration.

At Škoda, Zellmer has overseen the brand during a period of product and market expansion. Volvo Cars said Škoda delivered record results in 2025, followed by growth and record electric vehicle deliveries in the first half of 2026.

Håkan Samuelsson has led Volvo Cars during two separate periods, first from 2012 to 2022 and again since April 2025. He returned to the company to work on its long-term strategic roadmap during a challenging period for the automotive industry.
Eric Li, Chairman of Volvo Cars, said Zellmer's experience across premium and high-volume automotive brands would be relevant to the company's next phase.
Zellmer said Volvo Cars has a strong reputation for safety and a clear brand identity, adding that he looks forward to working with the company's teams as it develops its next chapter.
The leadership change comes shortly after Volvo Cars outlined a new strategic roadmap and announced plans for 13 new cars between now and the end of 2030.
